channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Ronan Guillou Grant #4 · Eyes Wide Open
item.description: Eyes Wide Open's fourth Ronan Guillou Grant is a €4,000 photographic creation grant for one professional photographer from Europe or from a country on the southern shore of the Mediterranean, to make an engaged project about people and the marine world in and around Sète, the Étang de Thau and the Gulf of Lion in Occitanie. ENTRY IS FREE: no fee appears on the call page, in the regulations PDF or on the online application form, and the form has no payment step - applications travel by email. THE DEADLINE IS NOT END OF DAY: the regulations state the dossier must arrive "no later than 15 November 2026 at 6 p.m. (Paris Time)", and the form repeats "between 1 October and 15 November 2026, at 6:00 p.m. (French time)". THE AWARD: "a grant of €4,000 (including €3,000 in remuneration and €1,000 in per diem)", plus two return journeys to Sète and accommodation there during the residency; all other production costs are borne by the grantee. The winner has five months to make the work, including a cumulative two months on site that may be split into two stays between February and June 2027, scheduled jointly with the organisers. The result is presented in September 2027 at the Musée de l'Étang de Thau in Bouzigues as part of the second FLOW Biennale (18 September-31 October 2027). ELIGIBILITY - THE TWO SURFACES DISAGREE AND THE BINDING ONE IS WIDER: the signed regulations (Article 4) say the call "is open to European photographer candidates or photographers from a country bordering the Mediterranean", while the call page and both language blocks of the form say "the southern shore(s) of the Mediterranean"; the regulations are the document participation accepts, so a photographer on the non-European northern or eastern Mediterranean rim is admitted by the text that binds. No age limit; independent or represented by an agency, collective or gallery. Duos may not apply. The programme is "open to all forms of photographic creation with preference given to original documentary, post-documentary and fine-art approaches"; an eco-responsible approach - in subject, production technique or presentation - counts as an assessment criterion but is not required. The project must keep a link to the Occitanie region, thematic, geographic, historical, cultural or symbolic, without having to cover the whole region. HOW TO APPLY - TWO STEPS, BOTH REQUIRED: fill in the online application form, then send one single PDF named SURNAME_FIRSTNAME_PROJECT TITLE via a SwissTransfer link (under 50 MB, valid one week) to the association's address, with the subject line "RGG #4_LAST NAME+FIRST NAME". The PDF holds a short biography and CV, a project statement of 3,000-6,000 characters with illustrations or a mood board if needed and any partners named, a portfolio of up to 25 MB, and the signed regulations. The regulations PDF's own figure for the statement reads 2,500-6,000 characters, so write to the stricter 3,000 floor. Applications may be in French or English. SELECTION is by a jury of the grant's organisers and experts in photography and/or the marine world; no juror is named on any surface. The winner is contacted first and announced in December 2026. READ THE RIGHTS CLAUSE: "The grant recipient assigns their copyright to the organisers until 31 December 2027 for uses that may be made of the selected 25 images exclusively within the framework of the Ronan Guillou Grants and the FLOW programme of which it forms part: exhibition, catalogue, communications, internet and social media." That is a time-limited, purpose-scoped assignment, not a permanent transfer, and it covers only the 25 delivered images. At the end of the residency the grantee owes the organisers at least 25 photographs with captions and a presentation text; sketches, notebooks, other multimedia or sound work are welcome alongside. The grant is named for photographer Ronan Guillou, from Roscoff, a humanist observer of the marine world who died suddenly in 2022; it is supported by Sète Agglopôle Méditerranée, M28-Terres de culture, the Musée ethnographique de l'Étang de Thau, Hahnemühle and the Tomoé laboratory. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €4,000 + 2-month residency + Exhibition.

item.title: GradFoto 2026 · Ballarat International Foto Biennale
item.description: The Ballarat International Foto Biennale's GradFoto Award, running since 2020, is a free prize for photographers graduating in 2026 from a tertiary art programme in Australia or Aotearoa New Zealand. ENTRY IS FREE: the terms and conditions state "Entry is free." and the entry form carries no fee field or payment step. THE MEDIUM AFFIRMATIVE IS EXPLICIT AND WIDE: entries must "be a series of photographic works that have been substantially produced by photographic means, including analogue and digital photography, collage and mixed media", and the award is "open to emerging contemporary artists from selected institutions whose artistic practice includes photography". You submit a series of 1 to 20 images with an artistic rationale; the project must be finished and must have been executed or resolved after 1 January 2026, within the graduating year. Images are jpegs at 2000 px on the longest edge, 300 dpi, between 2 MB and 10 MB, named with artist, series and sequence number, with one file flagged _HERO for social media use; watermarked photographs are not accepted. The entry form also carries a field the call page and the terms never mention: "If you would like to include a video work(s) as part of your submission, please share up to 5 minutes as a link via a sharing website" - so a moving-image component can travel with the series, outside the 20 upload slots. ELIGIBILITY IS AN INSTITUTION LIST, NOT AN OPEN GEOGRAPHY: applicants must be 18 or over as of the closing date, must be graduating a diploma, bachelor, honours or masters programme in 2026, must be "living in Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand", and must be at one of the named institutions - AND THE SURFACES DISAGREE ON WHICH. The call page and the entry form's institution dropdown each name exactly 40 and agree name for name; the binding terms and conditions name 38, omitting Sydney College of the Arts and TAFE Queensland, both of which are selectable on the form. If you are graduating from either of those two, ask before you build the application: the terms reserve to the Biennale and the judges "absolute discretion in determining the eligibility of an entry based on their interpretation of the Terms and Conditions of entry". Anyone whose school is on no list is invited to email the Education & Public Engagement Coordinator about future rounds. THE JUDGE IS NAMED: Bindi Vora, interdisciplinary artist, Senior Curator at Autograph in London and Associate Lecturer at UAL, whose curatorial practice explores postcolonial histories, diaspora and reinterpretation through photography and lens-based practices. Up to 20 finalists are selected from the digital files and shown in the GradFoto 2026 online exhibition; the overall winner and the People's Choice are then judged from the exhibited work. PRIZES: one non-acquisitive cash prize of AUD $1,000 (inc. GST if applicable) to the overall winner, who also gets a consultation with Ballarat Foto to build industry connections, and a separate AUD $500 non-acquisitive cash prize for the People's Choice Award, voted by the public from 11 December 2026 to 1 February 2027. RIGHTS: copyright stays with the photographer, but each finalist grants Ballarat Foto, its touring partners and sponsors a non-exclusive, perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use the photographs, likeness and name, with attribution, to advertise and promote the award and the Biennale, in this and future years, with no fee or royalty. Finalists are contacted by 10 December 2026, the online exhibition and overall winner are announced 11 December 2026, and the People's Choice winner on 5 February 2027. Ballarat Foto states it is open to alternative application formats to improve the award's accessibility and gives a phone number and email to arrange them. — Deadline: November 22, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: A$1,000 + A$500 People's Choice + Online exhibition.

item.title: Open Summer Exhibition 2027 · Plas Glyn-y-Weddw
item.description: Plas Glyn-y-Weddw, the gallery and arts centre at Llanbedrog on the Llŷn Peninsula - an 1857 mansion that has housed an art gallery since 1896 - is rebuilding its annual Summer Exhibition as a fully open submission from 2027 onwards. Until now participation was by other routes; from this edition "all artists wishing to exhibit must submit their work through the online application process." The show is described as an "annual mixed-media showcase celebrating creativity from across Wales and beyond". PHOTOGRAPHY IS NAMED, AND IN THE GUIDELINES RATHER THAN THE WEB PAGE: "This open exhibition is for visual art only. We welcome submissions across a wide range of visual art disciplines, including painting, drawing, printmaking, photography, sculpture, ceramics, textiles, mixed media, and other visual art practices." The same clause excludes written work, film, video, animation, music, sound works and performance. ELIGIBILITY IS WIDE: applications are welcomed from artists of all backgrounds and levels of experience - professional, emerging, student, or "someone who creates in your spare time" - and applicants must be 16 years of age or over. There is no geographic restriction. THE DEADLINE HAS A CLOCK TIME: the guidelines FAQ states "March 1st 2027, 17:00", so entries close at 5pm, not end of day. FEES: £15 for up to 3 works, additional entries £5 per work, maximum submission 6 works - so a full six-work entry costs £30. AWARDS: a Judges' Choice Award of £1,500 plus a future solo artist show, and a Young Artist Award (Under 25) of £500. THE COMMISSION IS HIGH AND IT IS DISCLOSED IN THE GUIDELINES, NOT ON THE CALL PAGE: "Plas Glyn-y-Weddw charges a 43% commission (inc VAT) on all artworks sold during the exhibition. This commission is deducted from the final sale price." The format is an "off-the-wall" hang: selected works are available for immediate purchase and collection throughout the run, so the exhibition continually evolves as pieces sell. SIZE LIMITS: wall-based works maximum 1m², plinth or floor-based works maximum 60cm³. Submitted work must be complete at the time of submission and must be the actual work exhibited - substitutes and alternatives will not be accepted, and works differing from the submission in appearance or size may be rejected. Selection is by an independent selection panel. The exhibition runs 25 July to 3 October 2027, open 9:30-17:00 seven days a week with free entry, and there is a free public opening with refreshments to which friends and family are welcome. Artists need not be present. Promotion runs across the gallery's channels and printed material, and all works are viewable and buyable at oriel.org.uk. Applications go through a free CuratorSpace account. — Deadline: March 1, 2027. Fee: £15 for up to 3 works. Prize: £1,500 + Solo exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Regional Juried Exhibition · Hill Center Galleries
item.description: Hill Center Galleries' annual regional juried exhibition, open only to artists living in Washington DC, Maryland and Virginia, working in original 2D work in any medium — photography included. The selected show hangs January 18 to May 1, 2027 in the galleries of the Old Naval Hospital on Capitol Hill, a nontraditional venue where work hangs from a cable-and-hook Arakawa system; there are no size restrictions, and 14-foot ceilings in some of the gallery spaces accommodate large pieces. Juror for 2027 is Florencio Lennox "Lenny" Campello, curator of the 2025 "Women Artists of the DMV" survey show, critic, artist, art blogger and arts advocate. Prizes: First Place $1,000 plus an invitation to a spot in the 2027 Solo Artist Exhibitions, installed in the galleries in September 2027; Second Place $750; Third Place $500; plus Honorable Mention certificates. Submitted work must date from 2023-2026 and must not have been shown at Hill Center Galleries before. One entry per artist, 1-5 pieces, with a short artist statement and a description of each piece. All artwork must be available for sale: selected artists sign the Hill Center Galleries consignment agreement and the galleries retain a 30% sales commission, with no price changes allowed after the deadline. Work must be delivered to and collected from the Hill Center in person — no shipping either way. A limited number of entry fee scholarships is available on enquiry. — Deadline: November 5, 2026. Fee: $45 for up to 5 pieces ($10 each additional). Prize: $1,000 First Place + $750 Second Place + $500 Third Place + Solo exhibition invitation.

item.title: 2027 Artist Residencies at Alchemy Art Center · Alchemy Art Center
item.description: Alchemy Art Center runs a seasonal artist-in-residence programme on San Juan Island, Washington, for artists working in four named mediums — ceramics, printmaking, fiber art and DARKROOM PHOTOGRAPHY. Three 2027 cohorts: Cohort I (teaching focus) May 1 - June 9, 2027; Cohort II (community art focus) June 13 - July 21, 2027; Cohort III (community art focus) July 25 - September 8, 2027. Every cohort carries a work exchange of 15 hours per week — teaching adult classes, leading free park workshops, mentoring young people, studio managing, special projects — and a personal living stipend of $100 per week. Cohort I is the shoulder-season teaching residency and wants artists established in one of the four studio practices who are experienced teaching adult-level classes; the centre names alternative photo processes among the classes it would like proposed for 2027. Cohorts II and III support the Artists in Community programme through the busy summer. Professional opportunities available to residents can include a final exhibition in one of Alchemy's gallery spaces, a portfolio documentation project with the San Juan Public Library, an artist talk in partnership with the San Juan Islands Museum of Art, and a chance to sell work in the shop. Residents are encouraged to work across all of Alchemy's focus areas regardless of their own expertise. ACCOMMODATION IS RUSTIC AND COMMUNAL: individual woodland sleeping cabins reached by dirt paths, furnished with a bed, mosquito net, lamp, outlet and rack, with shared bathroom and kitchen space for up to 10 people — the call asks plainly that applicants be comfortable living semi-outdoors in Pacific Northwest weather. The campuses sit about 5 miles outside town with no public transit, so a vehicle helps. Applications for 2027 opened October 5, 2026 and close December 7, 2026 at 11:59pm Pacific; acceptances are announced in early February 2027. — Deadline: December 7, 2026. Fee: $15. Prize: $100/week stipend + Accommodation.

item.title: Illuminated · Gallery 114
item.description: Gallery 114 - a member-owned, cooperatively managed artist collective in Portland's Pearl District, running since 1990 - is calling for work for Illuminated, a community juried exhibition "celebrating the magic of light in the late days of Winter". The show is produced in conjunction with the Portland Winter Light Festival (February 5-13, 2027) and is an official programme of that event, receiving promotion and other benefits from it. The brief is open as to medium and specific about the theme: work must use light as a conceptual or physical component, which "could include chiaroscuro, luminescent environments, atmospheric or diffused lighting, referencing spiritual or sacred spaces, or elements within the piece that are lit or illuminated. No limitations--just show us your interpretation of Illuminated." MEDIA: "All 2 and 3-dimensional media are welcome" - photography is eligible, and the light theme suits it. ELIGIBILITY IS REGIONAL AND PHYSICAL: open to artists in the NW Oregon and SW Washington area, 18 or older, who can hand-deliver and collect work in person - all artworks must be HAND DELIVERED, with nothing accepted by any mailing service. Delivery is Friday January 29 or Saturday January 30, 2027; pickup Saturday February 27 or Sunday February 28. The exhibition hangs in the gallery's North Gallery, opens on First Thursday, February 4, 2027, 5-8pm, and closes Saturday February 27; a Guest Artist Meet and Greet runs Saturday February 20, 1-3pm, and the gallery opens on Fridays and Saturdays during the Winter Light Festival. A Juror's Award for Best of Show is presented at the opening reception. 2D work is limited to 48x48 inches and must have secure professional hanging hardware; 3D limits depend on mounting (wall-mounted 24x36 inches, free-standing to 36x36x72 inches, pedestal to 12x12x24 inches). Any lighting apparatus in the work must be safely incorporated and battery power is encouraged over plug-in, as the gallery's outlet capacity is small. All work must be for sale. Up to 3 images for the base fee; images must be at least 200 dpi and 1200 px on the longest side, named first-initial-lastname-title-medium-price.jpg. — Deadline: November 29, 2026. Fee: $35 for 3 submissions ($5 per additional, maximum 6). Prize: Exhibition + Juror's Award for Best of Show.

item.title: 3rd Gonzaga Triennial: Inland Northwest Juried Landscape Art Exhibition · Jundt Art Museum at Gonzaga University
item.description: The Jundt Art Museum at Gonzaga University holds this juried landscape show every third summer, and the 3rd Gonzaga Triennial runs May 22 to August 28, 2027 in the Jundt Galleries and the Arcade Gallery, with a reception and awards evening on Friday, May 21, 2027, 4-7pm. The show "seeks to present the diversity and dynamism of contemporary artistic activity in the Inland Northwest while celebrating the relationship between art and the local landscape" - a theme the prospectus frames with Chief Seattle, Spokane Garry, James Thomson and W. J. T. Mitchell on landscape as "a medium of exchange between the human and the natural". MEDIA: submissions "may be in any media", with no specific size limitations for two- or three-dimensional work (gallery space is limited); photography is eligible, though every placed award winner in 2018 and 2024 worked in paint or mixed media (the museum states no medium for its honorable mentions). Selection and awards are made by Wes Jessup, Executive Director of the Northwest Museum of Arts and Culture in Spokane, and Paul Manoguerra, Director/Curator of the Jundt Art Museum and a juror for the first two Triennials; they judge on artistic quality and merit, adherence to the landscape theme, the artist's educational and professional achievements, and observance of the application rules. PRIZES: first $1,000, second $500, honorable mentions $250 each, with sponsored awards possibly available. ELIGIBILITY IS STRICTLY GEOGRAPHIC AND MUST BE PROVEN: artists must be residents of one of 20 named Washington counties (Adams, Asotin, Benton, Chelan, Columbia, Douglas, Ferry, Franklin, Garfield, Grant, Kittitas, Klickitat, Lincoln, Okanogan, Pend Oreille, Spokane, Stevens, Walla Walla, Whitman, Yakima) or 10 named Idaho counties (Benewah, Bonner, Boundary, Clearwater, Idaho, Kootenai, Latah, Lewis, Nez Perce, Shoshone), and must upload proof - a mortgage or rental statement, driver's license or utility bill - with the application. "No exceptions to the residency requirement will be made." Up to three works may be submitted, one image each showing the entire work, plus a biography covering major educational and professional achievements. All submissions must be completed works: no incomplete works, conceptual works or project proposals. WORK IS NOT FOR SALE in this exhibition and must stay on site for the whole run; Gonzaga insures everything in the museum's custody and handles all installation, with placement and lighting at the museum's discretion. Artists deliver to the museum loading dock May 12-14, 2027 and collect August 30-31, 2027. The first edition (2018) drew almost 4,000 visitors; the second, postponed by the pandemic to 2024, drew more than 3,500. — Deadline: February 1, 2027. Fee: $25. Prize: $1,000 First Place + $500 Second Place + $250 Honorable Mention.

item.title: I Guess That's Why They Call It The Blues — Fall Student & Member Showcase · The Art Center
item.description: The Art Center at Johns Creek, Georgia opens its Fall Student & Member Showcase on the blues - colour, music, mood and everything in between. Taking its title from the Elton John song, the show asks for "artwork that embraces blue as color or idea": indigo skies, cobalt and cerulean; grief, longing, loneliness, healing, resilience, quiet contemplation; the musical tradition of the Blues; water, sky, atmosphere and nature; memory and nostalgia. Abstract or representational, subtle or bold, humorous or heartbreaking. The call quotes Langston Hughes ("Blue songs are songs of hope. You sing them because you're hard up, but not because you're beaten") and Kandinsky on blue calling "man towards the infinite". PHOTOGRAPHY IS NAMED: eligible media are mixed media, ceramics, drawings, fiber art, printmaking, painting, collage, digital art, photography and sculpture. ELIGIBILITY IS A MEMBERSHIP GATE, NOT A JURY: the show is open to current members of The Art Center and to students who have taken a class there in the last 12 months - students and members are judged separately - and the page links its membership offerings for anyone whose membership has lapsed. ENTRY IS FREE AND ACCEPTANCE IS LARGELY GUARANTEED: each artist may submit two works (students may submit two works from each class they are currently enrolled in), and "All artists will be guaranteed acceptance of one work." AI WORK IS NOT ACCEPTED: "All artwork must be an original creation of the submitting artist, AI work will not be considered." There are monetary awards, ribbons and other recognitions, presented at the Awards & Reception on November 13, 2026 at 6:30pm. The exhibition runs October 26 to November 20, 2026. Entry is by Google Form plus an email of your images to the curator; 2D work must not exceed 48 x 48 inches framed or weigh more than 20 lbs, works on paper should be framed with acrylic or plexiglass rather than glass, pieces must arrive dry and ready to hang with appropriate wire (sawtooth hangers are not recommended above 16x20 inches), and unframed canvases are accepted if back-stapled with painted edges and hanging wire. 3D work is capped at 50 lbs and 24 inches wide. Drop-off is October 19-20, pickup November 29-30. Artists keep 75% of any sale; The Art Center retains 25%. Work sent by mail must include a prepaid return label. — Deadline: October 9, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + Cash awards.

item.title: Contemporary | Abstract Exhibition 2026 · The Art Center
item.description: A juried national call from the Art Center in Dover, New Hampshire, for contemporary and abstract work, juried by painter Shiao-Ping Wang (MFA in painting, Queens College CUNY; represented by Barn Gallery in Ogunquit, Maine and Furchgott Soudiffe Gallery in VT (the prospectus's own spelling); residencies in the US, France, Spain and Canada and at the Surf Point Foundation in Maine). WHAT THE PROSPECTUS SAYS ABOUT MEDIA, EXACTLY: "All Contemporary | Abstract works will be considered" - it enumerates no media at all, so there is no photography affirmative and no photography exclusion on this call page. The reason it is listed here is the org's own programme: the Art Center runs Across America as a national photography exhibition, and its 2026 gallery season included solo shows by photographers. Read the brief as a theme, not a medium: abstract and contemporary photographic work fits the stated brief, but if you want the gallery's own confirmation for a particular process, ask before you pay. THE TERMS, from the ArtCall prospectus: open to all artists in the U.S.; up to three pieces per entry; Art Center members enter free with an up-to-date membership through the end of the exhibit, non-members pay $30 for up to three submissions; work must be framed and ready for installation, with canvas paintings exempt if the edges are finished; work needing assembly or a complex install must come with written instructions and reference photos. THE CONDITION TO WEIGH: "All artwork must be for sale and cannot be removed during the exhibition." On any sale the artist receives 70% and the Art Center retains 30%. That flat 30% is the good news in the terms: the gallery's own membership page (theartcenterdover.com/artists/apply.php) prices the member commission at 30% and states "Non-member commission is 40%", so this prospectus charges every entrant the member rate. The Art Center also reserves the right to photograph accepted work for publication and publicity. No cash awards are named anywhere on the prospectus; what comes back is the hang, a named juror's selection and a seven-week run. Accepted work is delivered between October 27 and November 4; shipped work must include a prepaid FedEx or UPS return label (the prospectus recommends pirateship.com for this). Exhibition dates November 9 - December 31, 2026 at 1 Washington Street, Dover. — Deadline: October 23, 2026. Fee: $30/3 works (members free). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2026–27 Vermont Scholastic Art & Writing Awards · Brattleboro Museum & Art Center
item.description: The Brattleboro Museum & Art Center is the Vermont affiliate of the Scholastic Art & Writing Awards, the national teen programme run by the Alliance for Young Artists & Writers, and this is its 2026-27 regional call. WHO CAN ENTER: students in grades 7-12 (ages 13 and up). BMAC holds the Vermont Art Region AND the Vermont Writing Region for the whole state, so a Vermont teen's entry is judged here. The work must have been made in calendar year 2026, except that senior portfolios may contain work from the previous year. PHOTOGRAPHY IS A NAMED CATEGORY WITH ITS OWN WORK CAP: the programme's FAQ states there is no limit on the number of works you may enter "with the exception of Photography and Portfolio", and that "Each participant is allowed to enter 16 works in the Photography category". Portfolio entries, which carry the larger scholarships, are open only to current seniors. WHAT YOU GET: Vermont entries are judged regionally by teams of experts in art and writing; Gold Key, Silver Key and Honorable Mention regional awards are exhibited at the Brattleboro Museum & Art Center from February 19 to March 6, 2027. Regional Gold Key work advances to national adjudication, where BMAC's page says "students can win college scholarships and other prizes" without naming an amount - but the programme operator does, on the same FAQ that carries the photography cap: a scholarship committee "awards sixteen $12,500 Gold Medal Portfolio scholarships (eight writing and eight art)", with "Additional $2,000 scholarships ... given to students earning Silver Medal Portfolios". Portfolios are grade-12-only, so for a Vermont senior photographer that $12,500 is the real ceiling of this call; for everyone else what comes back is the regional award and the February hang. Neither surface names a notification date. THE MONEY: the Alliance charges $15 per individual entry and $40 per portfolio, and runs fee waivers across all regions "for teens who cannot afford the entry fee", partly funded by BLICK Art Materials; it asks families who can afford the fee to pay it. The submission portal opened October 1 and closes December 15, 2026. AI: the programme permits AI tools as an aid during making - brainstorming, outlining - but deems ineligible "any entered work for which the final product is itself AI-generated", defined as work created automatically from prompts with minimal or no human interaction; that counts as a plagiarism violation and an award can be withdrawn after the fact. — Deadline: December 15, 2026. Fee: $15/entry, $40/portfolio (fee waivers available). Prize: Exhibition + $12,500 / $2,000 portfolio scholarships.

item.title: Issue 3: Art and Photography Submissions
item.description: Wandering Lights is a small online magazine that "publishes literature, art, and photography biannually", in March and September, and has two issues out already - Issue One (August 2026) and Issue Two (fall 2026, 127 pages). This is the reading window for Issue 3: submissions open October 1 and close December 1, 2026, and Issue 3 publishes on March 1, 2027. PHOTOGRAPHY IS NAMED AND PUBLISHED, not inferred. The Submittable form for this call enumerates it: "This includes works of acrylic or oil painting, watercolor, oil pastel, sketch, digital art, and photography. In your submission, please indicate the precise medium of your submission." Issue Two's contents credit seven photographs by name - including a 35 mm negative print - the masthead carries an Art and Photography Editor, and the cover image "Lunar Light" was photographed by a contributor. COVER ART IS A SEPARATE SHOT: the form says some submissions "may additionally be considered for cover art", and if you want to be read for it the brief is "artwork that captures light in any form - a lamppost, a glimmer, sunlight, a candle". WHAT YOU MAY SEND: up to five pieces in the Art category, and no more than five pieces TOTAL if you mix categories, one submission per period. Work must be previously unpublished; simultaneous submissions are welcome, with a request that you email promptly if a piece is placed elsewhere. Images go as direct files at a minimum of 300 PPI; every submission needs a third-person bio of 50 words or less. THE FEE: this art and photography form carries NO fee on Submittable. The magazine's submissions page says "We have moved to Submittable and charge a small fee to cover business costs. At this time, we are not a paying market" - that fee is on the sibling Issue 3: Literary Submissions form, which lists $3.00; the art and photography form's fee column is empty. Check the form before you commit, because the page sentence reads as if it covers both. RIGHTS ARE CLEAN: "you are granting Wandering Lights first serial rights to publish and archive your work at wanderinglightsmag.com. After first publication, all rights revert back to the author" - the magazine only asks for an acknowledgement as original publisher if you republish. Nothing is paid to contributors. EDITORIAL STEER: the magazine is Christian-owned and says so, while stating that it "welcome[s] both religious and non-religious work" and that a submission "does not need to be Christian-based"; the editors ask for work read through what they call "a lens of redemptive storytelling" after Eve Sedgwick's reparative reading - "acknowledgement of the darkness in our world through the persistent lens of hope" - and say they do not want anything that reads like a sermon or devotional. They decline hate speech, plagiarism, defamation, content condoning violence, and the overly vulgar. Response comes within a month of the window closing. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: Free (art & photography form; the literary form is $3). Prize: Publication.

item.title: Neuwerk Lake Residency 2027
item.description: The first edition of a new studio residency and exhibition on Lake Constance, run by the Neuwerk cooperative with the Cultural Office of the City of Konstanz. Neuwerk eG is an unusual host: a cooperative of craftspeople, trades, service providers and freelancers working under the motto "Gewerbe tragt Kultur" (business carries culture), which "creates space for artistic work, cultural exchange and new ideas". The programme was initiated in 2026 and starts in 2027, and the setting is part of the pitch - Konstanz sits in the corner where Germany, Austria and Switzerland meet, and the residency's name takes up the lake. WHAT IS ACTUALLY PROVIDED, in the organiser's own list: two to three months in the studio with accommodation and utilities included; exclusive use of the 116 square metre studio at the Neuwerk, which the site states is step-free; a following exhibition of two to three months at venues in the Konstanz region - for this first residency the vaulted cellar of the Kulturzentrum am Munster in the old town; 1.000,00 EUR exhibition remuneration; a separately negotiated budget for realising the exhibition, which can cover installation, design and publicity; promotion of the show and a vernissage; and introductions to the art and cultural scene of Konstanz and the Lake Constance region. There is no application fee. BE CLEAR ABOUT WHAT IS NOT PROVIDED, because the organiser is: "Reisekosten, Lebenshaltungskosten, Versicherungen und Honorare werden nicht ubernommen. Die Kunstlerinnen und Kunstler mussen ihren Aufenthalt selbst finanzieren konnen" - travel, living costs, insurance and fees are not covered, artists must be able to finance their own stay, and a funding overview for the stay is a required part of the application. The studio and the accommodation themselves cost nothing. Residency is compulsory: on-site presence "ist ein wesentlicher Bestandteil des Programms", with short absences of a few days possible by prior arrangement. Dates for this first round: studio 1 May to 30 June 2027, vernissage mid-to-late June 2027, exhibition June to September 2027. A public accompanying format - an artist talk, open studio, workshop or studio conversation - is part of the residency and the resident helps design it. Photography is covered by the organiser's own affirmative: "Die Neuwerk Lake Residency ist offen fur alle Sparten der zeitgenossischen Kunst und Gestaltung" - open to all disciplines of contemporary art and design. Who it is for: professionally working, up-and-coming artists with an independent practice in contemporary art or design; applications are open regionally, nationally and internationally, from the Lake Constance region, the German-speaking countries, Europe and beyond; sufficient German or English is required; there is no age limit, though the programme is aimed in particular at artists at the start or middle of a professional career. Selection is by a jury drawn from Neuwerk eG, the Kulturamt Konstanz, artists from the Konstanz region and further cooperation partners, judging artistic quality and independence, the quality and feasibility of the planned project, what the residency would mean for the artist's development, the potential for exchange and cultural mediation, and the contribution to the diversity of the programme; no individual jurors are named and "Die Juryentscheidungen werden nicht begrundet" - decisions are not explained. Applications are taken only through the online form on the residency's own site, in German or English, as PDFs: at most 10 MB per document, portfolio at most 25 MB, 32 MB in total, comprising the completed form, a motivation letter of at most two A4 pages describing and justifying the planned project, a proposal for the accompanying programme of at most one A4 page, an artistic CV, a portfolio of selected work from the last two to three years, proof of registration and an identity document (passport and any residence documents for non-EU applicants), and the funding overview. Incomplete or late applications are not considered. Deadline 31 October 2026, with selection and offers in early December 2026. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 2–3 month residency + exhibition + €1,000.

item.title: Open Call 2026 · Teatergalleriet
item.description: An open, free call for exhibition proposals at a Swedish artist-run gallery that has been running since 1984. Teatergalleriet publishes the call in Swedish and English side by side: "Teatergalleriet in Kalmar is a non-profit, artist-run association that has presented solo and group exhibitions in our gallery in central Kalmar since 1984. We showcase a broad range of artistic practices of a professional standard and create space for diversity, new perspectives, and artistic exploration." The association was founded by working artists, and its stated aim is to give practising artists the chance to exhibit in Kalmar and to build public interest in art and craft. The call itself enumerates no media at all; what settles whether a photographer belongs here is the gallery's own exhibition archive, and it does, if thinly - Emelie Carlen's SIRENS' SONG (October 2025) is listed with a "Fotogram" (photogram) installed on the upper floor alongside a video projection and ceramics, so camera-less photographic work has been shown in this programme. The rest of the archive runs to embroidery, tapestry and painting, printmaking, cartographic drawing and sculpture, so a photographer should read this as a genuinely open programme rather than a photography venue. THE TIMELINE IS LONG AND THE GALLERY SAYS SO PLAINLY: applications are reviewed in January 2027 with outcomes notified in February 2027, and because "Teatergalleriet's exhibition programme is planned approximately one year in advance, successful proposals may be scheduled for exhibition from 2028 onwards." What a selected artist gets is a show in the gallery at Olof Palmes gata 1 by Larmtorget in central Kalmar, plus this commitment: "For artists who are offered an exhibition, Teatergalleriet undertakes to apply for exhibition remuneration through Sveriges Konstforeningar (The Swedish Art Associations)" - applied for on the artist's behalf, not guaranteed. There is no entry fee stated anywhere on the call and no cash prize. THE BINDING TERMS SIT ON A SEPARATE PAGE, NOT ON THE CALL: the gallery's "For utstallare" (For exhibitors) page carries a VILLKOR (conditions) block the call never mentions. Two items cost the artist money - "Vi tar 30 % inkl moms av forsaljningen av verk for att driva galleriet" (the gallery takes 30% including VAT of any sale of work, to run the gallery), and "Fraktkostnader och boende for konstnaren ska tackas av utstallningsersattningen", i.e. shipping and the artist's accommodation are to be met out of that exhibition remuneration rather than on top of it. The exhibitor is responsible for mounting the show, though the gallery's intendent can assist; against that, the gallery produces and pays for a poster and fly-posts it in Kalmar, invites the press to a viewing and invites its members to the vernissage, and it lists the sound and moving-image kit it lends - a 49-inch 4K monitor, a Full HD projector, speakers, headphones, media players, microphones and a 400 W PA. The same page records that the selection body meets once a year, at the turn of the year, and that it may ask a shortlisted applicant for further material. Applications go by email to the gallery as one single PDF of no more than 10 MB containing a CV of at most one page, an artist statement or presentation of at most one page, an exhibition proposal with ideas for the use of the gallery space of at most four pages including images, and a portfolio of at most ten pages. The deadline is 1 November 2026. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The River We Call Home · Brattleboro Museum & Art Center
item.description: A free, curated two-museum group exhibition marking the 75th anniversary of the Connecticut River Conservancy, organised by the Brattleboro Museum & Art Center with the Conservancy and the Connecticut River Museum. The brief is about a watershed as a lived-in place rather than scenery: the exhibition "honors the Connecticut River watershed as a place of wonder, belonging, and relationship-one that sustains both human and natural communities", and asks artists to reflect "a legacy of love and stewardship through artistic interpretations of the river as a home". Suggested entry points include the river "as a place of beauty, reflection, belonging, or identity", "Inhabitants of the watershed, great or small", "Relationships between people, wildlife, and water", "Change over time-ecological, cultural, or personal", stewardship and "Daily life, recreation, or quiet moments along the river". Readings may be "literal or abstract, historical or modern, celebratory or contemplative". Photography is named in the accepted media: "All media will be considered, including but not limited to: Painting, drawing, printmaking, Photography and digital media, Sculpture and installation, Fiber, textile, and mixed media, Assemblage or found-object work." THE GATE IS GEOGRAPHIC, NOT A RESIDENCY RULE: the call is open to artists who "Live, work, or have a meaningful connection to the Connecticut River watershed (in New Hampshire, Vermont, Massachusetts, or Connecticut)" and who can deliver or ship work to either institution; artists at all career stages are encouraged, and collaborative and interdisciplinary work is welcome. Selected work hangs in two linked shows at riverside venues: the Connecticut River Museum in Essex, Connecticut, February 13 to May 30, 2027, with an opening on March 25, and the Brattleboro Museum & Art Center in Brattleboro, Vermont, July 10 to October 31, 2027, with an opening on July 10. Artists may state a venue preference but "The curators will determine in which venue selected work will be displayed." Up to three works may be entered; the official Wufoo entry form carries exactly three work blocks, each with one required image and one optional detail image, plus a 250-word artist statement about your connection to the watershed and a 100-word bio. A curatorial panel reviews every submission, no jurors are named, and notification is due by December 4, 2026. There is no entry fee on any surface. There is also no promised award: BMAC says only that "Sales information, honoraria, or insurance details (if applicable) will be provided upon acceptance", so treat an honorarium as possible rather than published, and note that "Artists are responsible for delivery and retrieval of artwork unless otherwise noted" and that selected work "must be delivered ready to hang/display". BMAC itself is an independent, non-collecting contemporary art museum near the confluence of the Connecticut and West Rivers; it runs a standing Patrick and Marcelle Leahy Fund for Photography, and the Connecticut River Museum is accredited by the American Alliance of Museums. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Benton Fall 2026 · Associated Artists of Winston-Salem
item.description: A juried, themeless call for the Salem Foyer on the main floor of the Benton Convention Center, part of a curated fine-art series the Benton runs in partnership with Associated Artists of Winston-Salem, the artists' association founded in the city in 1956. AAWS is blunt about what the venue is and who walks through it: "Hosting countless events, conferences, and meetings from C-Suite and corporate businesspeople, the Benton Convention Center is a great venue for exposure." There is no required theme. The distinguishing feature is scale — the foyer is "well-suited for very large 2D art", and the call explicitly frames itself as "an excellent opportunity for very large 2D work which may not always be practical and allowed in other exhibits", with limits of 10 feet in height and 8 feet in width and a 50-pound ceiling per piece. Photography is affirmatively named in the accepted media: "All 2-dimensional fine art media accepted for selection", and separately, "Hand-pulled prints, original digital prints and photographs are all acceptable"; printed reproductions of paintings and drawings are not exhibited. The show is genuinely selective rather than first-come — members may submit up to six works for consideration, no more than four will be taken from any one artist, and roughly 15 to 25 pieces in total are chosen from digital images by a committee of AAWS jurors, who are not named. Work previously shown at the Benton is ineligible, though work entered and not selected in an earlier round may be re-entered. Entry is $20 for up to six works and is members-only: AAWS membership is bought online at $75 a year, or $20 for high-school students over 15 and college students, and is not itself juried — the general level lists "Entry into all exhibitions, including highly-renowned juried shows". Two constraints a photographer should weigh. First, the venue imposes content rules: "No nudes, and nothing controversial, i.e., nothing political religious, or potentially offensive to members of the general public." Second, there is no cash award of any kind — what comes back is the hang, from October 26, 2026 through the fall into mid or late January 2027. Entries close October 12, 2026, with acceptances sent no later than October 16 and drop-off and installation in person on October 26 between 9am and noon; pick-up is mid to late January, date to be confirmed. Sale prices are not displayed in the foyer — an AAWS plaque directs enquiries to the association — and artists set their own prices, receiving 70% with AAWS retaining a 30% commission plus 7% North Carolina sales tax. Accepted images are retained for publicity during the show and may be archived and used on the AAWS website. — Deadline: October 12, 2026. Fee: $20 for up to 6 entries. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 32nd Arts North International 2027 · Hopkins Center for the Arts
item.description: The 32nd edition of Arts North International, a juried physical exhibition open to living artists anywhere in the world, shown at the Hopkins Center for the Arts on historic Mainstreet in Hopkins, fifteen minutes from downtown Minneapolis, and supplemented by a virtual tour. Photography is named in the accepted media alongside painting, ceramics, drawing, textiles and fiber, glass, mixed media, pastel, printmaking, sculpture, digital drawing/painting/sculpture (no video) and watercolour and watermedia. More than $10,000 in awards is available: a juror-selected Best of Show of $3,000, two Awards of Excellence of $1,000 each, two Awards of Merit of $500 each, first, second and third in the medium-specific categories, and additional sponsor-selected special awards of $100 and up. Work must be original and completed since January 1, 2024, and may not have been shown in a previous Arts North exhibition; copies, class work and prints reproducing work in other media are not considered. Wall-hanging work is capped at 60 inches wide including the frame, and multi-part works are accepted only when mounted in a single frame or on a common base. Entry is $39 for three images or entries and $6 for each additional, to a maximum of ten images; three is also the minimum, so a single artwork still has to be shown in three views. At most three artworks may be selected. Applications close November 30, 2026 at 10:59pm Central; artists are notified by December 11, 2026. The exhibition runs January 16 to February 27, 2027, with a reception on the opening Saturday from 4 to 6pm. Accepted work is delivered free in person on January 9, 2027, or shipped to arrive between December 14, 2026 and January 8, 2027 with prepaid return label(s) enclosed, so an entrant who ships pays both legs; early in-person drop-off by appointment costs $25 per artist. Accepted work must stay up for the full run, and work listed for sale is sold through the centre, which retains a 30% commission. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: $39 (3 entries) + $6 each additional. Prize: $3,000 / $1,000 / $500 + Exhibition.

item.title: AAP Magazine #62 Travels · All About Photo
item.description: The 62nd printed issue of AAP Magazine takes Travels as its theme: "Reflect on your past or current adventures, expand our horizons from the four corners of the globe!" The editors ask for travel photographs "near and far, to the edge of the earth and to the places perhaps known only to you", and are explicit that the camera does not matter — "whether you're hauling around a view camera and a tripod or just pulling a mobile phone out of your back pocket". All genres, capture types, colour and black and white, traditional and non-traditional photographic and digital post-production processes are welcome, but what the magazine wants is a portfolio rather than one-off frames: photographs are judged individually in a blind first round and then as a unified group as they could be published, and "only a unified group of photos will be published in AAP Magazine". Work already published in AAP Magazine cannot be entered again. Up to 40 images may be entered and no minimum is set. Twenty-five photographers are chosen: $500 first place with an exclusive interview, $300 second and $200 third, and the next twenty-two, ranked 4 to 25, are finalists — all 25 are published in AAP Magazine Volume 62: Travels, receive a free copy of the printed issue, which is sold and distributed through Blurb, and keep a permanent place in the online Winners Gallery. The single juror is Sandrine Hermand-Grisel, the photographer, curator and editor who co-founded All About Photo in 2013. Entries cost $30 for the first three images through October 16, 2026 inclusive, rising to $35 for the first three after that date, with $5 for each additional image either side of the cliff — so a 40-image entry costs $215 early or $220 after. Files are JPEG, 72 dpi, longest dimension no more than 1,200 pixels, under 2 MB, with no watermarks. The FAQ says the call is "open to all individuals age 18 and older... professional and amateur photographers alike", while the binding Rules page sets the bar at "the age of majority in their jurisdiction of residence" and adds that the competition is void where prohibited, so check your own jurisdiction. The competition opened October 3, 2026 and closes November 10, 2026; judging runs November 14 to December 15, 2026. No notification date is stored here because the organiser's only one is impossible: both the call page and the Rules page say winners are notified "around January 1, 2026", ten months before the competition opened. Entrants grant a non-exclusive licence scoped to promoting the competition and photographers retain full copyright in every entry. — Deadline: November 10, 2026. Fee: $30–$35. Prize: $500/$300/$200 + Publication.

item.title: 39th Annual Culture & Agriculture Exhibition · Gallery Q
item.description: A national juried exhibition at Gallery Q, an artist-owned gallery in downtown Stevens Point, Wisconsin, running March 3 to April 29, 2027 and "celebrating our connection to the land and the art of farming since 1985". Work must be inspired by agriculture, "whether representational or abstract, and may include rural landscapes, farm life, or broader agricultural themes and issues"; the organisers describe an exhibition that moves "from the land and livestock to the laborers, tools, and traditions" with styles "ranging from representational to abstract". Open to all artists 18 and older, with work "created within the past five years" that represents the artist's current body of work. The accepted-media sentence is a dimensionality list rather than a medium list — "All two- and three-dimensional media, digital art, and video art are welcome" — so photography is admitted as two-dimensional work but is nowhere named in the prospectus, and a photographer entering should expect to be juried beside painting and sculpture. Awards total $2,850 across eight prizes, itemised in the prospectus as Best of Show $1,000, People's Choice Award $500, 1st Place $450, 2nd Place $350, 3rd Place $250 and three Honorable Mentions at $100 each; the People's Choice "will be selected at the conclusion of the exhibition". The online jury runs February 2–5, 2027 with notifications on February 7; final award selections are made in person on March 3–4, 2027, after the juror has seen the installed show, and "all exhibition and award decisions are made solely by the juror" — Gallery Q membership "provides no preference or special consideration". The 2027 juror is Roberta Condon, an award-winning Wisconsin artist, Master Circle pastelist with the International Association of Pastel Societies and Signature Member of the Pastel Society of America, whose American Pastoral series "explores the changing Midwestern agricultural landscape and the loss of the family farm"; she won Best of Show in the 2026 edition. Up to two works may be entered for the $30 fee, and artist statements are published in the exhibition, online catalog and marketing. Costs if selected sit with the artist: physical work must arrive February 24–27, 2027, wall-hung work wired and ready to hang (no easel-back or sawtooth frames), in durable reusable packaging with a prepaid, pre-addressed return shipping label enclosed — "artwork arriving without a prepaid return shipping label will not be installed in the exhibition" — and the artist insures the work in transit, though Gallery Q insures it from arrival through pickup or return. Accepted video art is delivered as a file and is not shipped. Sales are split 60/40 in the artist's favour. One clause to diary: unclaimed physical artwork left beyond 30 days after the exhibition becomes the property of Gallery Q. — Deadline: January 31, 2027. Fee: $30. Prize: $2,850 in cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Tallgrass Artist Residency 2027
item.description: A free-to-apply, ten-night residency in the tallgrass prairie, run since 2016 as a programme of the Kansas Arts Commission. Artists are housed at Matfield Station in Matfield Green, Kansas — a community of about fifty people, twenty miles from the Tallgrass Prairie National Preserve and home to a number of artists and community builders. The residency exists "to create connection and conversation across the Great Plains through engagement with the prairie ecosystem", and the organisers welcome "applicants from all backgrounds and career levels, media and practice", naming visual artists alongside writers, performers, composers, landscape architects and social practitioners, so a photographer applies on the same footing as anyone else. Residencies run in consecutive ten-night blocks between April and September 2027. Each artist receives lodging for the ten nights, a $650 stipend from the Kansas Arts Commission for travel and materials — reimbursed after the residency is completed, not in advance — and a connection to staff at the Tallgrass Prairie National Preserve, who may grant special access on request. Artists travelling from 700 or more miles away as the programme's one "ecoregion exchange" resident receive an extra travel stipend. What is asked in return is substantial and worth reading before applying: a public programme during the two weeks, daily Instagram posts documenting the experience, a written reflection for the residency website afterwards, and a commitment to share post-residency work at a time and venue agreed with staff. Artists arrange and pay for their own transport — a reliable vehicle is described as essential given the rural setting and the twenty-minute drive to the nearest groceries — and buy their own food, though cooking and eating utensils are provided in every room. There is no dedicated studio space: each artist’s apartment has a table and chair, and other local work spaces may be arranged with advance notice, depending on what the artist needs. The programme prioritises artists who currently live in a place that is ecologically prairie or grassland, with one residency period each year reserved for an artist from outside that ecoregion; it does not accept applications from international residents, or from artists who have held the residency before. Applications opened 1 October 2026 and selected artists are notified on 15 December 2026. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 2-week residency + $650 stipend.

item.title: Oh My, Octopi! · The Firefly Artists
item.description: Winter theme show at The Firefly Artists, the Northport, New York artist cooperative founded in 2011 and now fifty resident members strong at 90 Main Street. The theme is the octopus: "Take a dive into the mysterious depths where eight arms create endless possibilities." The gallery's application for this call names photography directly - "All original media is acceptable, such as drawing, painting, photography, printmaking, mixed media, sculpture, collage, fabric work, glasswork, jewelry and digital media" - while "AI-generated art is not" eligible, nor is work made in a workshop or class. Artists from throughout the Long Island region are invited and the gallery says off-island submissions are fine, but hand delivery and pickup at Northport are required: work goes in on 10 or 11 January and comes out from 11 February. Cash awards of $150, $75 and $50 plus honorable mention; the exhibition runs 12 January - 11 February 2027 with a reception on 28 January. Accepted work must be framed or at the very least wired and ready to hang, no more than 36 inches on the longest side, and must be for sale, with the gallery taking a 35% commission. The gallery's two surfaces disagree on how much one artist may enter: the application says one piece for $35 plus up to two more at $5 each and prints three work slots, while the PayPal page prices a ladder up to eight images ($70). The lower figure is stored here - ask the gallery before paying for more than three. The application itself is a Google Form. — Deadline: December 15, 2026. Fee: $35 (first image) + $5 each additional, up to 3. Prize: $150 + $75 + $50.

item.title: Then & Now: A Legacy Exhibition · Artists of Palm Beach County
item.description: Artists of Palm Beach County closes its 20th-anniversary year by asking artists to show their own evolution: each submission is a pair of works, an earlier piece representing "Then" and a recent piece representing "Now", hung together with a statement of up to 150 words on how the two connect. The earlier work is not shipped - it is submitted as a high-resolution JPG and printed at 8 x 10 inches to hang beside the new piece, which must arrive ready to install and no more than 36 inches on its longest side including the frame. "Original artwork in all media is welcome, including painting, drawing, photography, mixed media, fiber, sculpture, ceramics, and other three-dimensional work", and artists at every stage are invited - "you do not need to have been creating art ... for 20 years". The APBC Exhibition Committee accepts or declines each pair as a single submission, judging artistic quality, presentation and the strength of the relationship between the two works. Cash awards of $150, $100 and $50. The show runs 5-30 December 2026 at HATCH1121 in Lake Worth, with work delivered in person on 3 December and collected on 30 December. All work must be for sale; members keep 75% of gross sales and non-members 65%. No work made with artificial intelligence, and no explicit sexual work, is accepted. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: $30 members / $40 non-members. Prize: $150 / $100 / $50.

item.title: PICTURE STORM · Manifest Gallery
item.description: Manifest, the artist-run 501(c)(3) creative research gallery in Cincinnati, calls for works about image overload. "Our lives are loud with pictures": the prospectus asks how we slow the stream, how we process too much information, how we tell a lie from the truth, and how we cope with having to take part, willingly and unwillingly, in making images - "as loving as exchanging a picture with a friend, as essential as producing and revealing an artwork or scientific discovery, as discomfiting as being photographed in public". PICTURE STORM is a call for work about multiplicity, reproduction, excess, archives, records, overload and navigating a world overfull of visual information, from a gallery that runs its own darkroom and photo facility and an international photography annual - though Manifest states that its juries "have no collective predisposition towards any particular kind or style of art". Open to everyone internationally in all traditional and non-traditional media, with no size limit beyond what fits through the gallery door and no restriction on when the work was made. Selection is two-part: "an anonymous several member panel of professional and academic advisors" scores the entries and passes its recommendations to the exhibit curator, who makes the final selections from the jury-approved pool. Every exhibiting artist receives a $50 honorarium with no strings attached, and one work in each of the season's nine exhibition periods takes a $1,000 Grand Jury Award decided by re-jury. The exhibition runs 22 January - 19 February 2027 and selected work appears in the season annual. Work must arrive ready to install and artists pay shipping both ways; sale is optional, and the gallery takes 30% on anything sold. The entry form takes up to twelve works, at $45 for the first three and $5 for each one after. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: $45 (3 images) + $5 each. Prize: $50 honorarium + $1,000 Grand Jury.

item.title: ARMATURE · Manifest Gallery
item.description: Manifest, the artist-run 501(c)(3) creative research gallery in Cincinnati, calls for works about structure - "the skeletal systems that underpin everything: the sketches, blueprints, designs, the plans that must be sketched with forethought before a project can begin - the engineering of thought and form". The prospectus reaches past architecture to the physical, economic and social structures that carry weight: "Like a bone, like a building's foundation, like a transit system, feats of architectural, agricultural, technological, and social engineering must be repaired and maintained to be depended upon." Work may itself be structural or may depict structure; the gallery says plainly that it is open to artists' own readings of the theme. Open to everyone internationally in all traditional and non-traditional media, with no size limit beyond what fits through the gallery door and no restriction on when the work was made. Selection is two-part: "an anonymous several member panel of professional and academic advisors" scores the entries and passes its recommendations to the exhibit curator, who makes the final selections from the jury-approved pool. Every exhibiting artist receives a $50 honorarium with no strings attached, and one work in each of the season's nine exhibition periods takes a $1,000 Grand Jury Award decided by re-jury. The exhibition runs 22 January - 19 February 2027 and selected work appears in the season annual. Work must arrive ready to install and artists pay shipping both ways; sale is optional, and the gallery takes 30% on anything sold. The entry form takes up to twelve works, at $45 for the first three and $5 for each one after. — Deadline: October 17, 2026. Fee: $45 (3 images) + $5 each. Prize: $50 honorarium + $1,000 Grand Jury.

item.title: Art in Action 2027 · CICA Museum
item.description: CICA Museum in Gimpo, South Korea invites artists, performers, designers and professionals in creative fields to propose a project for Art in Action 2027, the museum's cross-disciplinary presentation programme. Three things come with selection. Participants show work in the group exhibition Art in Action: Concurrent Show 2027 at CICA Museum from December 23 2026 to January 10 2027, with up to two works each; the museum's own curators and assistants print, frame and install photographs and 2D digital art at 10 x 15 or 10 x 10 inches (larger prints are possible on request, and additional fees may apply). Participants also present their project in a 10-minute pre-recorded, edited video at Art in Action: Live 2027, a one-day YouTube live-streaming event on January 10 2027, with sessions of four to six presentations followed by roughly 20 minutes of live Q&A; that presentation video is due December 23 2026. And presenters are featured in the book New Media Art 2028, expected as a full-colour paperback in December 2027. Submission is by email and costs nothing: a link to a three-minute video in which you explain the proposed project, plus a short bio. If the proposal is accepted, the artist is asked to contribute $30 USD toward event registration and $78 USD (or 110,000 KRW) per work toward exhibition processing and maintenance to confirm participation — the same per-work contribution the museum's other open calls use. Artists sending physical work pay their own shipping both ways; two-dimensional work should be no larger than 39 inches on the longest side and wall-mounted work no heavier than 10 kg. Selected presenters are notified on acceptance and register November 1-15 2026. The museum notes the schedule is subject to change. — Deadline: October 23, 2026. Fee: Free to submit; $30 registration + $78 per accepted work. Prize: Museum exhibition + publication.

item.title: Arty Rat Magazine Open Call — November 2026
item.description: Arty Rat is an independent art journal run from Vienna by curator Oleksandr Dyvnich, showcasing contemporary visual art, illustration and "bold creative voices from around the world"; the open call page addresses itself to "artists and photographers". This is the next rolling cycle: submission is free, open worldwide to applicants 18 or older, and you may submit up to six works as JPG or PNG, either through the form on the call page or by emailing the files. Selected artists receive a free digital copy of the magazine as a PDF, photographs of their printed magazine pages and a feature on the journal's Instagram; two selected artists have their work on the magazine covers, and one selected artist takes part free of charge in a group exhibition at The Names Gallery in Vienna — a show the call page dates only as "the end of August" with no year, while the organiser's separate Vienna exhibition page advertises a Names Gallery show on November 14-15, so which show that free place applies to is not settled on either surface. A participation fee applies only if the work is selected, and the organiser lists the options openly: €35 for publication in the magazine, €65 for publication plus an artist's page on the website with biography, statement and photographs of works, €100 for a curatorial review covering magazine and website, and €100 for the Vienna exhibition. The fee is non-refundable. The most recent issue, Issue 5, was published in September 2026. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: Free (€35–€100 if accepted). Prize: Publication.

item.title: Gathered VII: Georgia Artists Selecting Georgia Artists · Museum of Contemporary Art of Georgia
item.description: The seventh instalment of MOCA GA's biennial exhibition built on a single idea: Georgia artists choose Georgia artists. The museum describes the project as the one in which “the MOCA GA mission is fully realized … as artists are involved in all phases of the exhibition, including selection and review”, and the series has run since 2006 under three successive names — Within State Lines (2006, 2009), Georgia Artists Selecting Georgia Artists (2013, 2015) and, since then, Gathered. This round is the first to be staged in MOCA GA's new building by Mack Scogin Merrill Elam Architects. The jury is three Georgia artists named on the call, each with a bio on the museum's own jurors page: Hannah Israel, gallery director and professor of art at Columbus State University; Craig Drennen, a painter and 2018 Guggenheim fellow who teaches at Georgia State University; and Kelly Taylor Mitchell, an artist and educator working between Atlanta and San Juan. Photography is part of what this series selects on the museum's own account of the last round — the 2023 jurors “selected a diverse spectrum of artwork including sculpture, painting, photography, textiles and new media”, a show of 46 artists — and the call itself names no medium restriction at all: artists submit three recent works, each produced within the last three years and all of which must stay available for the full run, since a juror may take one piece or several. Images go as jpeg or png under 4 MB and no more than 4800 px on the longest side, new media (video, animation, motion graphics) as mov or mp4 under 25 MB or as a link, with a bio of up to 150 words and a statement of 50–100 words. Work must arrive installation-ready, in what the museum asks be professional-quality frames or mounting. Entry is $35 and up to $5,000 in cash awards is given out. Eligibility is strictly residential: home and studio address both within Georgia, and 18 or over. MOCA GA provides installation staff, pedestals, shelving, projectors and monitors, interpretive materials, press and social marketing, and a public opening reception; artists deliver and collect their own work and sign a museum loan form. Submissions close at midnight on November 1, 2026, selections are notified by December 11, work is dropped off January 7–9 and the exhibition runs January 23 – March 27, 2027, opening with a reception on the 23rd. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Up to $5,000 in awards + Exhibition.

item.title: The Aftermath Project 2026 Post-Conflict Grant
item.description: A single $25,000 production grant, free to apply for, from the project Sara Terry founded out of her own five-year body of work on the aftermath of the war in Bosnia: photography that tells “the other half of the story of conflict — the story of what it takes for individuals to learn to live again, to rebuild destroyed lives and homes, to restore civil societies, to address the lingering wounds of war while struggling to create new avenues for peace”. One winner is funded and four finalists are named. The brief is deliberately wide on geography and scale and narrow on subject: the conflict may be an international war, a rebel insurgency, an urban riot or violence between rural ethnic groups, and the Project says it generally looks for stories “no longer being covered by the mainstream media, or which have been ignored”; proposals about the aftermath of domestic violence or environmental disaster are turned away unless clearly framed as the aftermath of conflict. The 2026 letter, signed by interim executive director Andrew Cullen, notes that several recent recipients have worked on conflicts in Ukraine and Gaza that are still running, and that the grant exists so that we “should not look away”. This is a production grant for still photography — explicitly not a distribution grant for exhibitions or books, and grant money may not be spent on video or audio even where a project includes them. An application is a signed form, a two-page proposal opening with a one-sentence summary, a portfolio of up to 30 jpegs (1200 px on the longest side, 72 dpi, under 2 MB each, named LastName_1.jpg), a caption sheet and a two-paragraph bio, sent by WeTransfer, Drive or Dropbox to the Project's email; there is no budget requirement, and it is fine not to have started the project. Open to working photographers worldwide; full-time students are not eligible. Photographers keep all copyright. The winner is paid in three parts — half at onset, 40% at the interim report, the last 10% on delivery of twelve 16x20-inch or larger prints for the Project's archive — with the work due by January 1, 2028 and prints by May 1, 2028; the winner then makes at least 30 images, and finalists 10–15, available for possible exhibition, publication and the Project's lesson plans, with any press-use fee split 50/50 with the photographer. Applications close at midnight PST on December 1, 2026, with the winner and finalists announced by the end of that month. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $25,000.

item.title: Candelar 2027 · Candela Photographic Arts
item.description: A free, deliberately low-ceremony call from Candela, the Richmond photography gallery and independent book publisher that received 501(c)(3) status in May 2026 and reintroduced itself as Candela Photographic Arts “after fifteen years as Candela Books + Gallery”. The Candelar is exactly what the name suggests — a calendar — and 2027 marks its third run: a set of twelve 5×7 inch cards printed in-house on Hahnemühle Museum Etching paper. Candela asks for square photo-based images and frames the brief around the pictures that usually stay in the drawer: “your best and weirdest outtakes, b-sides, one-hit wonders, whatever you wish”. Seasonal themes are welcome but not required, and there is “no theme for the exhibition other than the use of photography”. Up to three square JPEGs at 1500px on the longest side may be entered, each with its title, year, medium and dimensions. Twelve artists are selected, and each receives a copy of the limited-run 2027 Candelar plus an artist’s spotlight on Candela’s website during their Candelar month; accepted artists are notified 23–24 October and the selection is announced Tuesday 27 October 2026. The entry form’s required terms state plainly what the exchange is: a selected image is printed for a calendar set that goes on retail sale, and the copy of that set is the artist’s compensation — no cash, and no transfer of copyright. Submissions are free and run from 29 September to 12 October 2026 at 11:59pm. Candela states no eligibility restriction and names no juror. The call page’s “Submit to the call” button opens a Google Form that requires a Google sign-in; the organiser’s own candelaphotoarts.org/candelar/submit page carries the full terms and a second, un-gated submission form. — Deadline: October 12, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication (print) + contributor copy.

item.title: VCCA Residency at Mt. San Angelo — Fall 2027 Period
item.description: VCCA's Mt. San Angelo campus in Amherst, Virginia takes applications three times a year, and the Fall cycle — for residencies scheduled September to December 2027 — opened on 1 October 2026 and closes 15 January 2027. Photography is one of the disciplines the organisation names outright, alongside poetry, fiction, nonfiction, playwriting and screenwriting, performance, film and video, drawing, painting, sculpture, installation art, music composition and cross-disciplinary art; emerging and established artists may apply, professional training and achievement are not required, and students enrolled in undergraduate, graduate or doctoral programmes are eligible, though projects of pure academic scholarship are not. Mt. San Angelo hosts around 400 artists a year in residencies of no minimum length and up to six weeks, with flexible scheduling. A residency includes a private bedroom with private en-suite bath, a private individual studio, three prepared meals a day and a community of more than 20 other artists in residence; photographers can also request use of VCCA's black-and-white darkroom during the application process. Read the money carefully: one $30 application covers both outcomes. VCCA puts the true cost of a residency at $240 per artist per day, asks accepted artists who do not receive a fully funded fellowship to contribute a minimum of $105 per day, and says it distributes a generous amount of financial aid every year — "if you are accepted and cannot pay at least $105 per day, VCCA will work with you in good faith to be sure you can come" — with reductions granted where true need is demonstrated. The same single application is considered for every fully funded fellowship the applicant is eligible for. Eight are listed for this Fall 2027 period, and the ones open to photographers are the Alonzo Davis Fellowship (American visual artists, two weeks plus a $500 honorarium, preference to those of African or Latin American descent), the Greater Opportunity Fellowships (any discipline, first-time VCCA residents, preference to artists who self-identify as people of color) and the Marian Treger Fellowship for Enduring Creativity (female-identifying visual artists emerging in mid-life and beyond whose paths have been detoured by chronic health conditions or disabilities, two weeks plus a $400 stipend). The application runs on SlideRoom and asks for the form, current work samples and a project description; letters of recommendation are not required. Application fee waivers are granted on request to Artist Services at least five days before the deadline. Artists may be in residence at Mt. San Angelo only once every two years. — Deadline: January 15, 2027. Fee: $30. Prize: Residency.

item.title: Life Framer — Solitude
item.description: The December round of Life Framer's twelve-part monthly photography award, judged by Johan Lolos, the Belgian–Greek landscape photographer known for sweeping, emotionally resonant images of the earth's wild places — Alpine peaks, the Gobi desert, the colour-infused Icelandic highlands, the jagged Greek coast. The brief asks for solitude in all its forms: the quiet clarity of a single person, the vastness of an empty landscape, the eloquence of negative space, chosen or imposed, expansive or intimate. Life Framer names a lone person in a crowd, an isolated animal in the wild, empty streets at dawn, minimalist scenes stripped to their essentials and objects set apart from their surroundings, running from contemplative portraits and sparse still life to sweeping vistas and subtle details. All genres and approaches are welcome — documentary, conceptual, candid, staged, studio, environmental — with new work or images from the archive. The award is open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers aged 18 and over; the organisers accept all types of photography from analog and digital devices including mobile phones and allow editing, post-processing, mixed media, collage and compositing provided photography is at the heart of the work, but state that they do not accept artificial intelligence or AI-generated imagery. Entry is priced by the number of images: $20 for one, $30 for three, $40 for six, or a $100 membership covering up to ten images in every monthly themed competition for twelve rolling months. The monthly first prize is $2,000, drawn from a $24,000 annual fund shared between the twelve monthly first-prize photographers, and the first- and second-prize images each month are exhibited in galleries around the world. Photographers retain full copyright, and Life Framer states it does not sell usage rights or use entries to train AI algorithms. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: $20–$100. Prize: $2,000.

item.title: Contemporary Horizons · TCG Gallery
item.description: Open-theme international call from TCG Gallery surveying the range of contemporary photography — documentary, portraiture, landscape, still life, abstraction, staged photography and experimental practice all welcome. The gallery frames the horizon as a place, a limit, a possibility or simply a way of thinking about what comes next; a literal horizon is not required, and it says it is equally interested in an intimate observation, a constructed scene, an unexpected formal relationship or a photograph that complicates an ordinary subject. "Contemporary" does not mean an image must have been made this year, follow a trend or depend on a particular camera or technique; suggested approaches run from people, identity and everyday life through places in transition and the built environment to film, alternative processes and experimental photographic methods. Digital, film, alternative-process and mixed-media photographic work is accepted, and previously exhibited work is welcome where the artist retains the necessary rights. Work is reviewed for visual strength, originality, photographic execution and its contribution to a coherent exhibition. Images generated by, or substantially altered with, generative AI are not eligible. Selected photographs appear in a curated online exhibition with artist and artwork information, running 1–31 December 2026, and remain in the TCG Gallery exhibition archive; the show may be promoted through the gallery's website, email and social channels.
