Submissions take up to three photographs per entry (one is enough, the other two slots optional), JPG at least 1200 pixels on the longest side, unwatermarked; multiple entries are permitted. Sales are optional and the gallery retains a 30% commission on work sold through it. The entry fee is $15 and covers up to three images, with fee waivers available on application — the gallery asks that waivers be requested at least 48 hours before the call closes, i.e. by November 18, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. The prospectus states plainly that it does not promise a printed book, an award or a sale. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: $15 (up to 3 images); fee waivers available. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: The Studios at MASS MoCA Residency — July–December 2027 · MASS MoCA
item.description: The Studios at MASS MoCA runs year-round on the museum's North Adams campus, hosting up to ten artists at a time for stays of two or four weeks, and the general open call for residencies between July and December 2027 is live. The programme primarily seeks visual artists — the organisation's own list names painters, sculptors, installation artists, photographers, video and new-media artists, fiber artists and printmakers — alongside writers in all literary disciplines, and artists from around the world are encouraged to apply. There is no application fee, and an artist must be at least 18 to apply; the organisation states that age is otherwise not a consideration in selection. A residency carries a private furnished studio with 24/7 access, a private bedroom in a shared apartment across the street from the museum, one communal meal a day with the other residents, a studio visit with a MASS MoCA or guest curator, optional open studios and presentations, a year of priority access to Assets for Artists career workshops, and three months of museum membership covering free gallery entry and free admission to the nearby Clark Art Institute. Read the money carefully, because one application covers two very different outcomes. The Studios charges rent: the standard rate is $650 per week, already subsidised against a stated operating cost of over $1,000 per week. On the same general application you can ask to be considered for financial aid, where artists "typically pay between $0 – $450/week depending on their needs," and for one or more fully funded fellowships. The General Fellowship is the one with no strings: it "will offer full fellowships that do not have geographic or demographic limitations… regardless of discipline or location," and funds all residency fees for up to four weeks in residence. A Fellowship for Black or Indigenous Artists and Writers funds all residency fees for up to four weeks. A Family Fellowship gives three parent-artists a fully funded August 6–23, 2027 residency with a private three- or four-bedroom apartment, up to two studios with 24/7 access, free reserved places in Camp MASS MoCA for children in grades 2–9, and a $600 stipend. Further partner fellowships are tied to specific communities — the Speranza Foundation (Lincoln City Fellows), YoungArts alumni, Art+Everywhere (MFA graduates of the Art Institute of Boston, Lesley University Art+Design and Clark University), and MFA or BFA fellowships with Brooklyn College, the Corcoran School, Maine College of Art and Design, MassArt, MICA, RISD, SAIC, Tyler at Temple, University of Oregon, UT Austin, Virginia Commonwealth University and Yale. You apply by ticking the relevant box on the general application; there is no separate form, and every applicant must first be accepted through the regular jurying process before a fellowship can be awarded. The organisation asks you to indicate whether you also want to be considered for a regular, partially subsidised residency if no fellowship is awarded — so an unsuccessful fellowship applicant can still be offered a place that costs money. Two routes do NOT lead to a funded place: the Early Application, which gives 9–15 months of lead time but is explicitly for artists planning to fully fund their stay at the $650 weekly rate and is not considered for financial aid or fellowships; and the Alumni application, where returning artists are not eligible for fellowships and pay $400 per week for four weeks or $450 per week for two. Applications close November 1, 2026 at 11:59pm EST. Calls open four times a year, two months before each deadline, with general-application deadlines on May 1 and November 1. The organisation says most residents do not pay the full rate: "The majority of our residents attend with full or partial financial aid." Up to ten images may be uploaded, each under 2MB, or a single PDF of no more than ten pages covering no more than ten pieces; video samples run to ten minutes in total. Notification takes up to three months and comes through Submittable. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Funded residency + $600 stipend (Family Fellowship).

item.title: FORECAST 2026 · SF Camerawork
item.description: SF Camerawork's annual juried exhibition of contemporary photography, presenting work by emerging and under-recognised artists. The jurors for this edition are Janet Delaney, the Berkeley-based photographer of South of Market and a 2020 Guggenheim Fellow; Omar Jason Farah, Curatorial Assistant at BAMPFA, previously at the Leslie-Lohman Museum and the Whitney; and Jonathan Mark Jackson, Assistant Professor of Photography at UC Santa Cruz and a 2026 Hellman Fellow, whose practice joins still photographs and prose around historic Black memory. They will consider all work within the expanded field of photography, from traditional to experimental, with a focus on recently completed, thought-provoking projects. Up to five artists are selected for a group exhibition at SF Camerawork's gallery at Fort Mason Center for Arts & Culture in San Francisco, running November 21, 2026 to January 9, 2027. One selected artist receives the $1,500 Juror's Choice Award and up to four more receive a $500 artist fee; selected work is featured across SF Camerawork's media channels, can be sold through the gallery on a 70/30 artist/organisation split, and brings opportunities for artist talks, interviews and audience engagement. Submit up to ten samples of finished, gallery-ready work (images up to 5MB; video up to 5 minutes or 250MB per sample, or a YouTube/Vimeo link), a brief project or artist's statement, and one of a CV, artist résumé or professional biography. Read the access route before you plan: there is NO application fee, but you must be a current SF Camerawork member, with membership valid through the closing date. The Community Membership artist rate is a sliding scale with a suggested contribution of $100 and options starting at $50, open to working artists including students (the full programme value is $250). Join first; the organisation then emails a link to the SlideRoom application, and current members have already been sent theirs. The cutoff is not end of day — applications close Sunday, October 11, 2026 at 5:59 PM PST. Selected artists are notified October 20, 2026 and gallery-ready artwork is due November 14, 2026. — Deadline: October 11, 2026. Fee: $50+ membership. Prize: $1,500 Juror's Choice + $500 artist fee + Exhibition.

item.title: RC50: A City in Focus · City of Rancho Cucamonga
item.description: Free call from the City of Rancho Cucamonga's RC Public Art Program for a citywide photography exhibition marking the city's 50th anniversary. An Art Selection Panel chosen by the City will pick 50 photographs, each digitally applied to display banners by a third-party vendor and installed in public spaces around Rancho Cucamonga through the anniversary year; selected images may also appear on the project's own website. Every selected photographer is paid a $200 stipend. The City invites photographers of all experience levels and the themes are left to the artist, framed around four prompts: Community (people and everyday moments, neighbourhoods and landmarks, celebrations and traditions), Rancho Cucamonga history, the topography of the land, and nature native to the region. One entry per applicant. Alongside the image, the application asks for a Community Connection Statement of up to 100 words answering "What does Rancho Cucamonga mean to you?" and a three-word completion of the prompt "My Rancho Cucamonga is…"; the statement is scored on how well it communicates the applicant's connection to the city and how closely the work meets the call's goals. Entry is free and the CaFÉ system carries no charge. Read four things before applying. First, the deadline can arrive early: the City states the window closes December 3, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. PDT "or earlier if 200 applications are received (whichever occurs first)." Second, the City's own prospectus states the geographic bar two different ways on the same page — the Artist Eligibility list says "Artist must reside in the Inland Empire region," while the Geographic Eligibility paragraph says "This is an open call, but preference will be given to applicants who work, reside, or attend school in the Inland Empire Region." Third, the rights terms: the artist retains copyright, but the City "owns all installed artwork and reserves the right to copy, reproduce and adjust the artwork as it sees fit, in perpetuity," and reserves the right to remove, replace or adjust the work for the duration of the project. Fourth, the display is not guaranteed in place or duration — banners go onto functioning equipment that may need repair or replacement, and the City issues "no guarantee… for the location or longevity of display." Content limits: no political statements or persons, no religious references or symbols, no copyrighted or trademarked material, no corporate branding, nothing offensive or obscene, and work must be appropriate for public display in civic spaces. Only original photographs are accepted and applicants pledge the image was not digitally altered from someone else's work; artists are responsible for obtaining consent from identifiable people in their photographs. Open to all ages, with parent or guardian permission for minors. Current City employees may not apply. Judging runs January 4–25, 2027 and artists are notified by February 1, 2027. — Deadline: December 3, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $200 stipend + Exhibition.

item.title: PURPLEHAZE PRINT 013 — Unscripted
item.description: Free open call for the Autumn–Winter 2026 printed edition of PURPLEHAZE, an independent Berlin magazine published by HAZE ART & MEDIA GROUP. The theme is UNSCRIPTED, and the editors put it like this: the image does not always begin with intention — sometimes it forms in the space where control loosens, where timing overtakes composition, and where the frame captures more than it can contain. They are looking for work that holds tension, presence and unpredictability, and say they are drawn not only to the captured moment but to work where the process, the material or chance itself leads the artist toward a result that could not have been planned in advance. Staged or not, what matters is whether the work carries the feeling of something uncontrolled. Photographers, painters, performance artists, installation artists and image-makers of all kinds are invited; the call is open to artists worldwide at any stage of their career. Submit up to 12 works or one cohesive series as JPEGs at a minimum of 2000px on the long edge and/or a link to a portfolio or website, with a project statement of up to 150 words and a short artist bio, by email to the magazine. Selected projects appear in the Autumn–Winter 2026 printed edition. On rights: submitting grants PURPLEHAZE non-exclusive rights to reproduce selected work in the issue, and all other rights remain with the artist. Work is reviewed by the PURPLEHAZE editorial team on a separate timeline from the magazine's general submissions, and selected artists are notified by October 15, 2026. Read what does and does not come back before you submit: the magazine's stated policy is that complimentary print copies are not provided for independently selected editorial contributions, and contributors selected through the editorial process receive a 20% discount on one preordered copy of the issue; the magazine also states that publication is never conditional on payment. Previously shared work is welcome for art and photography projects, including work already posted on the artist's own social media — the magazine states that a post on your own account does not count as prior publication. One scope limit to read before applying: the call is for independent editorial and artistic submissions, and projects centred on a single designer, brand, collection, campaign or commercial identity are handled separately through the magazine's partnership formats. — Deadline: October 11, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Fotofestiwal Open Program 2027 · Fotofestiwal
item.description: The Open Program is the submissions route into Fotofestiwal, the International Festival of Photography in Łódź, Poland — founded in 2001 as one of the first photography events in Central Europe, visited by more than 20,000 people, and run since 2016 as a collective with no director and no vertical management structure. There is no theme: the organisers say they are looking for artists and collectives with a distinctive personality and for projects that propose a bold and original way of looking at photography and the contemporary world. Work in any technique is accepted, and the call is open with no thematic, age or regional restriction. The jury selects six projects, which are then developed with Fotofestiwal's curatorial team and shown in an exhibition in Łódź in June 2027. Each of the six selected artists receives a €1,000 artistic fee, accommodation for the festival's main opening weekend, travel costs reimbursed up to €300, and a budget of up to €600 for producing the exhibition or transporting the work. At least one of the submitting artists is also nominated to FUTURES, the European platform supporting emerging photographers. The 2027 jury is Jana Johanna Haeckel, curator of the 4th photo+ Photography Biennale in Düsseldorf in 2027 and lecturer in the history of photography and exhibition-making at KASK & Conservatorium in Ghent; Marta Szymańska, a photography curator who has co-created Fotofestiwal for more than twenty years and was deputy director of the Archeology of Photography Foundation from 2014 to 2019; Francesco Rombaldi, curator, editor and book designer, founder of the Yogurt curatorial platform and of Charta; Roï Saade, artist, designer and curator, founder of Huwawa Publishing and director of Bound Narratives, working on visual culture, displacement and cultural production in the Middle East and North Africa; and Krzysztof Candrowicz, co-founder of Fotofestiwal, artistic director of the Hamburg Triennial of Photography from 2013 to 2018 and guest curator of the Ci.CLO Biennial in Porto from 2018 to 2024, who has juried the Rencontres d'Arles Discovery Award, the Deutsche Börse Photography Prize, Prix Pictet and World Press Photo. Submissions are complete photographic projects of 10 to 20 photographs, up to two projects per person, made through Picter. The fee is €15 per project, and the organisers state that a free submission is possible in justified cases — write to opencall@fotofestiwal.com. The call opened on October 1, 2026, closes on November 30, 2026, and results are announced on January 25, 2027. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: €15 per project. Prize: €1,000 artist fee + Exhibition.

item.title: The Room Next Door · Decagon Gallery
item.description: Online juried photography exhibition from Decagon Gallery on the space just beyond what we see — a door left ajar, a window lit across the courtyard, a hallway that turns out of sight, a voice through the wall. The gallery is looking for photographs that bring the viewer to the edge of a space they cannot fully enter: images where something is felt more than shown, where the frame stops just short of an answer, and where what lies beyond is left for the viewer to imagine. The organisers put the distinction plainly — the mystery should come from what the photograph withholds, not from what it hides. Thresholds, doorways, windows and reflections are welcome, as are interiors seen from outside and exteriors seen from within, neighbouring lives glimpsed at a distance, sounds, light and shadows arriving from somewhere else, and constructed or staged work that invents what waits on the other side. Documentary, conceptual and experimental approaches are all accepted; people may appear, but the subject is the space between here and there. Open to photographers worldwide aged 18 and over, with all photographic processes and styles welcome. First place receives $500, second $250, third $150 and two honorable mentions $50 each — $1,000 total in cash awards — plus a Human Presence Award granting free entry to a future exhibition of the recipient's choice; cash awards are limited to one per photographer, and a photographer selected for more than one receives only the award of greatest value. Selected artists get an online exhibition by Decagon Gallery, publication in a professionally designed exhibition catalog, and digital badges and certificates. Entry is $25 for up to 4 photographs and $5 each additional, with 10 image slots on the entry form. The juror has not been named: the organiser prints "Juror: TBD". Notification is January 1, 2027 and the exhibition runs January 10 to March 10, 2027. Photographers experiencing financial hardship, living in a war-torn area or residing in a sanctioned country can ask the gallery to waive the entry fee. — Deadline: December 15, 2026. Fee: $25 (4 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $1,000 in awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Black and White · Dusk Gallery
item.description: Themed group exhibition at Dusk Gallery in Santa Fe for monochromatic photography. The gallery's brief is short and direct: before color, there was light and shadow, and black and white photography strips a scene down to its essence, telling stories through contrast, texture and form. They are seeking powerful monochromatic work and ask for your strongest black and white pictures. Juried by Dusk founder Holly Hart, a fine art photographer whose work has been exhibited and published internationally; 26 images are selected for the gallery walls. The gallery covers the whole cost of presentation — one exhibition-quality print on Luster paper, custom framing in the gallery's signature 24×24 inch black museum-quality frames, and matting from its collection of precut white mats, sized by the gallery's team without cropping the original composition. Artists supply only a high-resolution JPEG between 500KB and 5MB with the longest side at 4,500 pixels. The exhibition runs February 5 to 26 with an opening reception on February 5; the year is not printed on the page, but the December 31, 2026 deadline and the two-week notification window place it in 2027. After the show the physical print is archived in the gallery's flat files for six months, photographers retain all rights to their images, and any sale splits 50/50 between gallery and photographer. Acceptance is emailed within two weeks of the deadline and high-resolution files are due within two days of that email. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. Entry is $40 for 5 images or $45 for up to 10, non-refundable and stated by the gallery to go towards operational costs. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: $40/5 images, $45/10. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Portfolio Review II · Fotografiska Emerging
item.description: The second edition of Fotografiska Emerging's open call for one-on-one portfolio reviews, giving image-makers direct access to Fotografiska curators who can help them understand where a project is headed and how it might be positioned for exhibition, editorial, or further development. Fotografiska says "the only requirement is the work itself: a visual project with a clear narrative" — a series that holds together, tells a story, and feels like it belongs as one body of work — though the terms add a few concrete ones: entrants must be at least 18, each project goes in as a single PDF of 5 to 15 images under 10 MB with a project description of up to 500 characters, and up to three projects may be submitted, one per entry. Applicants are also asked to say what kind of feedback they are hoping for. Participation is free of charge. Reviewers for this edition are Marie-Luise Mayer, Exhibitions Manager at Fotografiska Berlin, who has overseen the Emerging Berlin programme since 2023, and Sofia Liljergren, Exhibitions Manager at Fotografiska Stockholm. The submission deadline is 5 November 2026 at 6:00 PM CET and Fotografiska says it will contact everyone on 18 November; review sessions run on 26 November 2026 from 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM CET, online and in English over Microsoft Teams. Selected artists receive an individual time slot ahead of the review day, with the reviewer assigned rather than chosen, and slots cannot be rescheduled. Places are limited and each session lasts 20 minutes. Applicants are asked to confirm they are available on 26 November during those hours before submitting. Further editions are planned, including time zones suited to a wider global community. — Deadline: November 5, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: None listed.

item.title: Arts & Heritage Show · City of San Marcos
item.description: The Walkers' Gallery, in the City of San Marcos Activity Center, invites artists to its inaugural Arts & Heritage Show, exploring the artistic and cultural landscape of San Marcos, Texas. Artists may work in any style — literal or symbolic, abstract, or a reference to something personally meaningful — with the organisers noting that work carrying cultural flavour and colour will sit well beside the local heritage exhibits hung alongside it. All 2-D and 3-D media that can be safely hung on the walls or in the large windows are eligible, so photography qualifies; the only content restrictions are that work for this family-friendly public venue must be apolitical, non-violent and G-rated, with no nudity even if tasteful and artistic. There is no entry fee and no commission on sales, which are conducted directly between artist and buyer. Each artist may bring up to one large work 36 inches wide or more, or up to two medium or smaller works, with a limit of two entries per artist and a 30 lb weight limit; pieces must arrive ready to hang with hardware installed. This is not a juried show — the gallery reserves the right to limit entries to include as many artists as wish to enter, and placement is first-come, first-served. Artwork is delivered in person to the San Marcos Activity Center on Saturday October 24, the artists' reception is Friday November 20 from 5.30 to 7pm with music and refreshments, and work is collected on Saturday January 9, 2027. — Deadline: October 22, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: American Natural Landscapes Open Call · Soft Publishing
item.description: Open call from Soft Publishing, the Treviso-based independent publishing house producing contemporary photography books in limited editions, for its next title: photographs of the natural landscapes of the Americas, north and south. Colour or black and white are both welcome, and the organiser asks explicitly for natural rather than urban landscape work. Up to ten high-resolution photographs may be submitted, each at least 2000 pixels on the longest side, alongside the artist's name, email and Instagram handle, a biography of at most 20 words, a project statement or concept of at most 50 words, and full captions for every image. Entries go only through the publisher's Google Form, which requires a Google sign-in. Images generated by artificial intelligence are not accepted, and work depicting violent content is excluded. The call carries a submission fee at a rate the organiser discounts until 15 October 2026; the amount appears on neither the call page nor the form, which cannot be opened without signing in. Selected artists are published in the book and are offered a discount on ordering their own copies. The call names no age, nationality or residence restriction. Soft Publishing's shop lists its earlier titles — European Landscapes, Eastern European Landscapes, Northern European Landscapes, Contemporary Photography Around the World and Soft magazine n.00 — and its black-and-white open call closed in August 2026. — Deadline: December 18, 2026. Fee: Paid. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Flowers and Related Themes Open Call · Soft Publishing
item.description: Soft Publishing, the Treviso-based independent publishing house producing contemporary photography books in limited editions, invites work on flowers read as broadly as possible. The organiser's own examples run from a garden or a living room to fresh-picked or withered stems, flowers painted or printed on a dress, a flower-shaped vase, a chair whose shape evokes a blossom, a bloom held by a person or a cat playing in a flower-filled meadow — offered as inspiration rather than a list to follow literally. The call states that flowers have long been associated with femininity and asks artists to move beyond that convention and approach the theme from as many perspectives as possible. Photography is the first of eleven media the entry form lets an artist declare, alongside drawing and painting, video, collage, embroidery, sculpture, patchwork, paper art, clay, set design and design, with a free-text field for anything else; if the submissions are diverse enough the publisher says it would like to structure the book into chapters by interpretation. Up to ten images may be submitted through the Tally form, with higher-resolution files requested if the work is selected, plus a biography of at most 20 words, a project description of at most 50 words written in the third person, and a caption list matching the number of images uploaded. The entry carries a €7 submission fee, which the publisher says supports the project and the production of the publication. Finalists are selected by 15 March 2027. — Deadline: February 15, 2027. Fee: €7. Prize: Publication.

item.title: RBSA Friends Exhibition 2027
item.description: Annual exhibition giving RBSA Friends — artists at any stage of practice — a wall in the RBSA Gallery in Birmingham, one of the oldest art societies in the country, which was among the first to give its subscribers their own show. This edition spreads across both Gallery 1 and Gallery 2 and runs Thursday 7 January to Saturday 6 February 2027, with a preview evening on the opening night. Artists working in any media, including photography, may submit; selection is by digital image of the original artwork and every entry goes through the same anonymous process, judged by Honorary Curator Simon Conolly RBSA, Friends Coordinator Charles Weston RBSA and Linda Nevill RBSA. Friends may enter up to three 2D wall-hung works or up to four 3D plinth or freestanding works, with four works the maximum in any mix. Entry itself is free, but the call is only open to artists holding an active RBSA Friends subscription, which can be bought on the RBSA site at £47 a year (£42 by Direct Debit, £120 for three years, £190 for five) and is not itself selected for — and selected artists then pay a display fee of £15 for 2D works under 60cm or £23 over 60cm, due by 10 December and halved for artists aged 35 and under. Photographers should read the entry requirements closely: work must have been made in the past three years and must not have been shown at the RBSA Gallery before, reproductions of original works such as giclee prints are not accepted, every print including digital ones must be editioned with the edition size stated, and images created using AI are not accepted. All work must be for sale for the full duration of the exhibition, with the Gallery taking 35% commission plus VAT on anything sold, and up to six Highly Commended certificates are awarded. International artists may enter but carry their own customs paperwork and charges, and work that has to be couriered back incurs a £20 re-packaging charge. A catalogue of all selected works goes on sale through the run and into the RBSA Archive, and the Gallery runs events during the exhibition for Friends who want to apply to become an RBSA Associate. Entry deadline Tuesday 10 November, 4.00pm. — Deadline: November 10, 2026. Fee: Free to enter (RBSA Friends subscription £47/year); display fee £15–£23 per selected 2D work, halved for artists 35 and under. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: RENEWAL: Winter 2027 Juried Exhibition · Blue Mountain Gallery
item.description: Blue Mountain Gallery, an artist-run gallery of 45 years in New York City's Chelsea district, invites artists working in two- and three-dimensional media to submit to its 19th juried exhibition, on the theme RENEWAL — new beginnings, transformation and the possibility of change: shedding an old skin, a new season, a repaired or reinvented object, a fresh perspective, a moment of personal awakening. The juror is Orly Cogan, a New York artist at the forefront of contemporary fiber art since the late 1990s, trained as a painter at Cooper Union and MICA, represented by Robert Mann Gallery in New York for her photo-fiber work and by Tracey Morgan Gallery in Asheville for her mixed-media work. Accepted media are painting, drawing, printmaking, collage, mixed media, photography and sculpture in any medium; giclées and similar reproductions are not accepted, and the EntryThingy listing adds digital art to that exclusion where the prospectus does not. Selected work hangs in the gallery's Chelsea space 5–30 January 2027, accompanied by a fully illustrated catalog and promoted to collectors, critics and media — gallery exhibitions have been reviewed in Art in America, The New York Times, The New Republic and Hyperallergic. The gallery deducts no commission on sales: 100% of proceeds go to the artist, and BMG passes buyer enquiries directly to the artist rather than brokering sales. Open worldwide to artists 18 and over, except those currently represented by the gallery; artists must be able to ship (commercial carrier, arriving no earlier than 8 December and by 15–16 December 2026 — the prospectus gives both dates) or hand-deliver (17–18 December) to New York, and pay their own shipping, insurance and return postage. Work must arrive framed, wired and ready to hang, under Plexiglas unless hand-delivered. Artists retain full copyright; submission grants publicity use only, always credited. — Deadline: November 18, 2026. Fee: $45 for 1–3 works + $6 each additional (max 10). Prize: Exhibition + Catalog.

item.title: 2026 Open Call Award · The Independent Photographer
item.description: The October round of The Independent Photographer's monthly award cycle, and the one with no theme at all: "Your choice: street, travel, fine art, landscape, documentary, portrait, and more. In October, we invite photographers of all ages, backgrounds, and experiences to unleash their creativity and share their best images". Judge: Maggie Steber, the documentary photographer and Guggenheim Fellow who led a Pulitzer Prize-winning photography team at The Miami Herald, has been featured in 16 National Geographic stories, contributes to the VII Foundation, and holds the Leica Medal of Excellence, a World Press Photo Award and the Lucie Award. Total prize pool $3,000 — 1st prize $1,500, 2nd $500, 3rd $300, and $100 to each of the seven finalists. Winners and finalists have their work professionally printed and shown at the platform's annual group exhibition at PCB Gallery in London, with TIP covering all printing, installation and display costs, and are featured to an audience the organiser states as 995k+ on Instagram and 205k+ on Facebook; every entrant also receives a free online portfolio on the platform. Fees are tiered: $15 for 1 image, $30 for 3, $45 for 6, and there is no limit on the number of separate submissions. Judging is anonymous — "the selection process is done anonymously to ensure that each contestant is judged fairly and only based on their work". Photographers retain full copyright. AI-generated images are explicitly not accepted; otherwise any photography-based work qualifies, film, digital, smartphone, tintype or camera-less, with all post-production allowed provided the result stays photography-based, and diptychs accepted. JPEG or PNG, minimum 1200px on at least one side and under 10,000px in height or width, maximum 10MB per image. Open worldwide to entrants aged 18 or over; there is no age limit on the pictures themselves, though the organiser says it is "trying to promote new content". — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: $15–$45. Prize: $3,000 pool.

item.title: RC50: A City in Focus · City of Rancho Cucamonga
item.description: A free citywide photography exhibition marking Rancho Cucamonga's 50th anniversary, run by the city's own RC Public Art programme, "showcasing the people, places, and stories that define our community". An Art Selection Panel chosen by the City picks 50 photographs to be displayed in public spaces across the city — digitally applied to display banners by a third-party vendor, shown at community locations and events through the anniversary year and on the exhibition's own website. Each selected photographer is paid a $200 stipend. The city invites photographers of all experience levels; themes are left to the photographer within four prompts — community (people and everyday moments, neighbourhoods and landmarks, celebrations and traditions), the city's history, the topography of the land, and nature native to the region — and applicants also write a 100-word community connection statement and complete the prompt "My Rancho Cucamonga is…" in three words. One entry per applicant, free to enter. Open to all ages with parent or guardian permission for minors, but the application's eligibility block requires that the artist reside in the Inland Empire region (the call summary words this more loosely as a preference for applicants who work, reside or attend school there); current City employees are not eligible. Entries close December 3, 2026 at 11:59pm PDT, or earlier if 200 applications are received — whichever comes first. Judging runs January 4–25, 2027 and selections are announced by February 1, 2027. READ THE RIGHTS TERMS: the artist retains copyright, but "the City owns all installed artwork and reserves the right to copy, reproduce and adjust the artwork as it sees fit, in perpetuity", and no guarantee is given for the location or longevity of the display. — Deadline: December 3, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $200 stipend.

item.title: Photo Trouvée Virtual Artist Residency — Spring 2027
item.description: 10-week virtual residency led by Juliana Naufel and Twiggy Boyer, founders of Photo Trouvée Magazine, for artists who work with or are inspired by found or family photographs. Artists are invited to set goals, carve out time for their practice, focus on a project and connect with like-minded artists around the world; 6–8 slots are available. The programme runs weekly 60–90 minute live Zoom calls on Fridays at 1pm EST, a Writing About Your Work mini workshop on the artist bio and statement, an artist talk with a guest speaker, six group feedback calls (each artist gets live group feedback at least twice), small accountability pods, networking for future projects, lifetime access to call replays and a one-year digital subscription to the magazine. Open to artists and creatives from anywhere in the world and at any stage of their career, working in any medium as long as found or family photography informs the work; the calls are in English, but the organisers say they will work on solutions rather than let that limit participation. Participants commit to attending at least 80% of the live calls. The investment is a one-time payment of $650 or two payments of $330, non-refundable and payable in full before the first live call, and partial scholarships of 15%, 25%, 30% or another amount are available to a couple of artists. Applications are accepted until all spots are filled; the cohort's call dates are listed as TBD. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: $650. Prize: Residency.

item.title: Curator's Choice — Project Submissions · Art Fluent
item.description: Art Fluent's free, rolling call for whole projects to feature in its Curator's Choice series — "a spotlight of artist features, bringing you their words of wisdom and how they work through their creative process". The series is framed as a collective resource rather than a competition: "Learning from others brings us together as a community of artists and makers… This project is about inspiring others to make their thing and to change their world… It is about success, failures, fear, and courage, all wrapped up in the stories, the magic, and the practice." Six pages of past features are published on the Boston organisation's site. Open to all fine art mediums, with photography explicitly enumerated alongside oil, acrylic, watermedia, pastel, drawing, printmaking, mixed media, sculpture, fiber, wood, ceramics, glass, film/video and digital art; AI will not be accepted. Free to enter: send a third-person bio, a first-person statement and 8–10 jpegs that best represent your series in a zipped folder (a Vimeo link for video), named "Your Name_Project Submission", to the organisation by email with Project Submission in the subject line. A feature typically presents seven pieces. Art Fluent warns that because of the volume of projects it receives, you will only be contacted if it chooses to feature your work. — Deadline: October 8, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Online publication feature.

item.title: American Vision Scholarship · International Center of Photography
item.description: ICP's scholarship for photographers currently based in the United States, offering $15,000 toward tuition for the 2027–2028 academic year. Two awards go to students enrolled in one of ICP's One-Year Certificate Programs — either Creative Practices or Documentary Practice and Visual Journalism — against a published annual tuition of $12,500 plus a $60 application fee. The scholarship is open to any applicant currently residing in the United States; recipients are selected by ICP's Scholarship Committee on the strength of their application materials and portfolios, "with a focus on those who demonstrate a distinctive visual voice and strong potential in the field of photography". Both the programme application and the scholarship application must be submitted by March 1, 2027 to be considered; applications for the Fall 2027 admission cycle opened on October 1, 2026. Scholarships are available only to students enrolled in the One-Year Certificate programmes, not to part-time programmes or individual courses, and awards cannot be combined — an applicant may receive only one. — Deadline: March 1, 2027. Fee: $60 program application fee. Prize: 2 × $15,000 tuition scholarship.

item.title: Alberto Contreras Scholarship · International Center of Photography
item.description: ICP's scholarship honouring "the memory and creativity of Mexican photographer Alberto Contreras", covering full tuition and school fees for the 2027–2028 academic year for one recipient enrolled in ICP's onsite One-Year Certificate Program in Documentary Practice and Visual Journalism in New York — a programme whose published annual tuition is $12,500 plus a $60 application fee. Eligibility is "open to Latin American applicants currently residing in Latin America". Selection is based on application strength and portfolio; applications are reviewed by the ICP Scholarship Committee and finalists may be invited to a Zoom interview. Both the programme application and the scholarship form must be submitted by March 1, 2027; applications for the Fall 2027 admission cycle opened on October 1, 2026. Scholarships are available only to students enrolled in the One-Year Certificate programmes, not to part-time programmes or individual courses, and awards cannot be combined — an applicant may receive only one. — Deadline: March 1, 2027. Fee: $60 program application fee. Prize: Full tuition and school fees ($12,500 tuition).
